one_month_reasoning: Inside the window (to 2026-11-08): (1) Q3 2026 results. The date is not yet announced, but Generac has reported Q3 on the last Wednesday/Thursday of October (Q3 2025: notice Oct 15, release Oct 29 [17]), so a report around Oct 28 to Nov 4 is very likely inside the window. Consensus Q3 EPS is $2.43 and was cut by 14 analysts vs 3 raising in the last 30 days [7], so the residential weakness from a very quiet hurricane season (quietest since 2013, no US hurricane landfall in nearly two years until Isaias [15]) is largely in expectations; C&I/data center should be strong after the Amazon agreement [4] and peer data-center commentary [9][10]. The swing factors are the first explicit 2027 data-center revenue framing (Amazon 2027-28 deliveries of $2.4B [4]) and C&I margin, either of which can move the stock 10%+ either way. (2) Hurricane Isaias, forecast to make Gulf Coast landfall around Oct 9-10 as a Cat 2 with long-duration outage warnings [15]: a modest positive for home-standby lead commentary on the call. (3) Hyperscaler and Caterpillar/Cummins Q3 reports in late Oct/early Nov: read-through on data-center power demand. I have no directional edge on the print, so I keep the distribution nearly symmetric around today's price (median $226, a hair above spot after the Isaias/Amazon backdrop) with a one-month log-sd of 16.5%, slightly above annual vol/3.5 (56%/3.5 = 16%) because an earnings event is in the window.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a segment sum-of-the-parts on CY2027E EBITDA ($281: residential $667M x 12x + C&I $549M x 18x, less $1.06B net debt, 60.0M shares) and a P/E on horizon NTM EPS ($260: $13.81 x 18.8x blended segment multiple).

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Residential CY27E sales $2.67B x 25% EBITDA margin = $667M x 12x TTM EV/EBITDA = $8.00B; C&I CY27E sales $3.66B x 15% = $549M x 18x = $9.88B; EV $17.89B less net debt $1.064B = $16.82B equity / 60.0M diluted shares = $280.4. At the Oct-2027 horizon, trailing EBITDA is roughly CY2027, so TTM peer multiples are applied.

inputs_detail.derivation: Margins = segment adjusted EBITDA / external net sales from the segment table.
FY2025 $4.21B [3] x 1.165 (mid-to-high-teens growth guidance maintained [1]) = $4.90B; consensus $4.94B [7].

H2 = $4.90B - H1 $2.23B = $2.67B; residential is H2-seasonal and guided to high-single-digit growth, C&I to low-30s% growth with ~$450M data-center revenue in 2026 [1][2]; split H2 roughly $1.38B residential / $1.29B C&I.

Mid-single-digit growth: penetration only ~6.5% and dealer count up ~400 y/y [2][16], but outage activity >30% below baseline [2], a quiet 2026 hurricane season [15] and continued US residential solar/storage softness after 25D expiry [14] cap growth; assumes normal outage year in 2027.

FY26E C&I $2.36B + ~$1.3B incremental data-center revenue (2026 DC ~$450M [2] -> 2027 ~$1.75B = $1.35B backlog scheduled for 2027 [2] + ~$0.4B of Amazon's $2.4B 2027-28 deliveries [4][5] not in that backlog). Total CY27E $6.33B vs consensus $6.40B [7].
H1 2026 30.3% includes the ~$71M Q2 tariff refund [1]; consolidated guidance ex-refunds is 18.5-19.5% [1][2]; strip ~4-5 pts of refunds and seasonality -> ~25%.

H1 2026 13.9% [1]; large-genset installed pricing $450-600/kW vs $380-420/kW in 2023 [12] and pricing above Generac's business case [2] support improvement with scale; well below Cummins Power Systems' 24.5% [9], a mature-incumbent ceiling.
Residential dealer-channel durables: LII 12.2x, AOS 10.4x, CARR 18.4x TTM EV/EBITDA; 12x sits at LII, inside the range, reflecting weather-driven volatility of home standby.

Data-center power peers CAT 25.1x, CMI 15.2x, ETN 28.2x, VRT 35.0x, HUBB 19.9x, NVT 27.1x, POWL 26.9x (median 26.9x). 18x is inside the range but below the median because GNRC's C&I margin is ~15% vs ~25% at CMI Power Systems [9], it is the newest entrant in large gensets, and industry capacity is rising fast (Caterpillar adding 1.5 GW [10], Rehlko's new Kenosha plant [11], Generac tripling assembly capacity [2]).
Total debt ~$1,329M (48.3 + 32.1 + 1,249.0) less cash $264.9M at 6/30/26; held flat to the horizon, assuming FCF goes to working capital and buybacks.
59.06M outstanding [8] + ~0.8M option/RSU dilution (Q2 diluted 59.64M vs basic 58.82M [1]) + ~0.15M treasury-method dilution from the Amazon warrant (1.69M shares at $200.93, mostly unvested [4]).

FY27 consensus $12.67 [7] x 1.12: Amazon 2027-28 deliveries [4], capacity tripling over 12 months [2], large-genset lead times constrained through at least 2027 [12], and Alphabet guiding 2027 capex up 'significantly' [13]; tempered by capacity additions and residential cyclicality.

EBITDA-weighted blend: residential 55% at 14.5x (LII 14.4x, AOS 14.5x fwd P/E) + C&I 45% at 24x (below the 28-31x electrical cluster ETN 28.5x, VRT 30.8x, NVT 28.7x, POWL 29.7x, CAT 27.8x, for the same margin/new-entrant/capacity reasons as in the SOTP) = 18.8x. Peer median fwd P/E is 27.8x; range 14.4-30.8x.

bear.story: AI capex digestion or a genset overbuild in 2027: hyperscalers slow or reschedule orders as Caterpillar, Cummins, Rehlko and Generac all add capacity, so large-genset pricing rolls over and Generac misses its 2027 ramp. Residential stays weak with another quiet storm year. FY28 EPS ~$10-11 at ~14x.

base.story: Data-center revenue rises from ~$450M to ~$1.7-1.9B in 2027 on the $1.35B scheduled backlog plus Amazon; C&I margins improve toward mid-teens; residential grows mid-single digits on normal outages. EPS tracks consensus ($12.7 FY27) and the stock trades ~18x horizon NTM EPS, with some discount kept for cyclicality and capacity risk.

bull.story: Shortages persist through 2027-28 (lead times 18-24 months at incumbents), Generac converts tripled capacity into a $2.5B+ data-center run-rate, Amazon volumes move toward the $8B ceiling, and an active 2027 hurricane season revives home standby. FY28 EPS ~$16-17 at ~22x, closer to the electrical peers.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 14.4x (LII) to 30.8x (VRT); TTM EV/EBITDA 10.4x (AOS) to 35.0x (VRT). The set is bimodal: data-center electrical/power names (CAT, ETN, VRT, NVT, POWL, TT) at 28-31x fwd P/E, and residential/cyclical durables and engines (LII, AOS, CMI, CARR) at 14-18x. Forward EV/EBITDA could not be sourced, so ev_ebitda_fwd is null and the median shown is TTM EV/EBITDA (StockAnalysis).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Blended 18.8x horizon NTM P/E and an implied ~14.7x CY27E EV/EBITDA (12x residential, 18x C&I). Both are inside the peer range and below the median. GNRC trades today at 17.8x FY27 consensus ($224.94/$12.67) and 21.7x StockAnalysis forward P/E, with 22.7x TTM EV/EBITDA.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: There is no premium. The below-median multiple is a segment mix effect, not a discount argument: about 55% of CY27E EBITDA is residential home standby, which belongs with the 14-18x durables cluster because demand swings with outage activity (2025-26 outages >30% below baseline, quiet 2026 hurricane season). The C&I piece sits below the electrical cluster because its EBITDA margin (~14-15%) is well below Cummins Power Systems (24.5%), Generac is the newest large-genset entrant, and capacity is being added across the industry, which threatens 2028+ pricing. I would move the C&I multiple toward the peer median only if C&I margins reach about 20%.

thesis_break_reason: $150 is ~11.8x FY27 consensus EPS and below the $173 Aug-Sep 2026 trough set before the Amazon agreement. Trading there would most likely mean the data-center ramp has broken: hyperscale orders deferred or cancelled, Amazon/second-hyperscaler volumes not converting to backlog, or large-genset pricing collapsing as industry capacity arrives. It could also mean residential suffers a structural decline rather than a weather lull. Ordinary volatility would not get there.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscale data-center capex into 2028, when the $1.35B 2027 backlog and Amazon's initial $2.4B rolls off
Industry capacity additions (Caterpillar +1.5 GW, Rehlko Kenosha, Generac tripling assembly) against a 2028 pricing reset
Whether C&I segment margins (~14% H1 2026) can rise toward the ~25% that Cummins Power Systems earns
Residential outage activity and hurricane frequency; home standby demand is weather-driven and 2025-26 has been well below baseline
US residential solar/storage weakness after the 25D credit expired at end-2025 (Enphase US revenue still falling, -3% q/q in Q2 2026), which hurts Generac's energy technology products
Tariff refunds versus potential higher tariffs (Q2 included ~$71M of refunds)
Execution of a 3x capacity ramp (engines are sourced; packaging partly third-party)
reasoning: Company basics come from the Q2 2026 release and call [1][2]: sales +11%, C&I +29%, $1.6B data-center backlog with $1.35B scheduled for 2027, 2026 data-center revenue ~$450M, and a path to triple assembly capacity in 12 months. Since then the September Amazon agreement [4][5] added ~$2.4B of 2027-28 deliveries, up to $8B, with a warrant struck at $200.93. In my industry lane, the value chain confirms demand is still tight. Cummins Power Systems grew 19% with 24.5% EBITDA margins on data-center standby demand and raised its full-year outlook [9]. Caterpillar's power generation retail sales rose 72%, with its CEO saying 'no one is slowing down' [10]. Trade research puts >2.5 MW genset lead times at 18-24 months through at least 2027, with installed pricing up from $380-420/kW to $450-600/kW since 2023 [12]. Hyperscaler 2026 capex is ~$725B, and Alphabet guides 2027 'significantly' higher [13]. The same chain also flags the medium-term risk: every incumbent is adding capacity (CAT 1.5 GW restart [10], Rehlko Kenosha [11], GNRC 3x [2]), so 2028+ pricing is the key bear risk. The residential side is soft. Outages are >30% below baseline [2], 2026 is on pace for the quietest Atlantic season since 2013 [15], dealers reported softer 2025 industry sales [16], and Enphase's US revenue kept falling in Q2 2026 (-3% q/q) after the 25D credit expired [14]. Valuation: the SOTP gives $281 and P/E gives $260, for a blended fair value of $270 (+20%). Both are deliberately below the 27.8x peer median because over half of EBITDA is weather-driven residential and C&I margins are about half of Cummins'. Consensus FY27 EPS has risen from $11.26 to $12.67 in 90 days [7]. For the ladder I used three lognormal scenarios: bear $150 (25%, log-sd 0.32), base $250 (50%, 0.26) and bull $370 (25%, 0.26). This gives a mean of ~$255, a median of ~$248, P(>= today's $225) of ~60%, and an overall log-sd of ~0.43. That is below the trailing 56% realized vol, which was inflated by deal and macro jumps (e.g. a June Iran-strike selloff [6]), but tails are kept fat (1.4% below $90, 1.4% above $562). Research limits: Twelve Data fundamentals/statistics and Alpha Vantage overview endpoints were plan-restricted; sec.gov refused scripted access so filings were read via WebFetch; forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not obtainable; Rehlko's own release returned 403. No option or implied-volatility data was used.
